model.description: The `model` block `keryx review tier` printed for this dispatch (Step 6) — pasted verbatim, never composed by hand. `tier` is the mechanical vocabulary the command emits (`light`/`standard`/`deep`), never a model name. `provider`/`model` are present when the command resolved a concrete model; `inherit: true` replaces them when it could not, meaning the dispatch runs on the caller's own model. Field naming matches `model` in `contracts/subagent-dispatch.schema.json` and the object `keryx review tier --json` prints under its own `model` key.

inherit.description: Run this dispatch on the caller's own model. Present in place of `provider`/`model`, never alongside them, when `keryx review tier` could not resolve a concrete model.

model_discovery.description: What `keryx review tier` discovered and how it ranked it, as printed. Not re-validated field by field here — that contract lives in `contracts/subagent-dispatch.schema.json`.

round.description: Which review round this dispatch is. Round 1 is the first review of a change; every later round is reviewing work produced in response to the previous one.

is_fix_round.description: True when the diff under review was produced to answer earlier findings. A fix round without the earlier findings is the failure this field exists to stop: the reviewer cannot tell whether a fix is complete when it does not know what the fix was answering.

prior_findings.description: Every finding from earlier rounds on this change, with what the fix claimed about each. Eleven rounds across two flows were dispatched without this, and twice in a row the fix repaired the site the finding named while leaving its siblings — which the NEXT round then found. A reviewer that can see the earlier finding and the claimed disposition can check the claim.

finding.description: The finding as reported, including its class_scope when it carried one. Deliberately the normalized contract in src/gdskills/contracts/, not the bundled reviewer-output shape: a prior finding is one finding, and it is the same object the learning and ingest paths already consume.

claimed_disposition.description: What the fix round claimed. A claim, not a verified state — verifying it is the reviewer's job.

claimed_evidence.description: What the fix offered as proof: the test added, the mutation that went red, the command run.

metaproject.description: Shared project context, the same context `keryx flow init` already collects for an implementation flow. The review pipeline collected none of it for eleven rounds, which is why a recorded lesson naming the exact recurring failure never reached a reviewer.

memory.description: Accepted memory entries whose recorded scope intersects the changed files or modules. Accepted only: a draft entry is a hypothesis, and putting one in front of a reviewer as project truth is how a wrong hypothesis becomes a wrong finding.

wiki.description: Wiki pages covering the architecture, domain rules or decisions the changed files participate in.

graph.description: Blast radius from `keryx gdgraph affected`, so a reviewer can see what a changed symbol reaches without reading the tree.
